mission: Mission 10T — Full Catalog Storage/CDN Decision Matrix

rks3CatalogContext.sourceFormatPolicy: Only HDWAV-sourced records enter the RKS3 Music Portal.
rks3CatalogContext.currentLocalAudioPolicy: public/audio/rks3 remains a protected local 30-record sample and must not become the full catalog host.

primaryRecommendation.decision: Use Cloudflare R2 as the first serious full-catalog audio storage candidate. Keep Bunny as the low-cost CDN backup. Keep AWS for later enterprise maturity. Use Vercel Blob/Supabase Storage for app-level files, not the main HDWAV catalog.

providerRankings.name: Cloudflare R2
bestFor: audio delivery with low egress risk
strengths: No egress bandwidth charges on R2 storage classes.
Strong fit for high-download media catalogs.
Good match for RKS3 because the audio catalog will grow beyond local Git storage.
risks: Needs bucket policy, custom domain, cache headers, and upload workflow.
Private/protected playback may require extra signed URL or worker logic later.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Best first-choice storage layer for the full RKS3 HDWAV catalog when moving audio outside Git.
providerRankings.launchUse: Use for full-catalog audio objects. Keep app metadata in repo/database and point audioSrc to R2 public/custom-domain URLs.
providerRankings.costPosture: Low egress-risk; request/storage costs still need monitoring.

providerRankings.name: Bunny Storage + Bunny CDN
strengths: Good for straightforward public media delivery.
Storage-to-CDN traffic is designed to work together cleanly.
risks: Not the same ecosystem depth as AWS.
S3-compatible migration story may be less central than R2/S3 depending on exact workflow.
Private access and advanced authorization need careful planning.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Strong backup choice if RKS3 wants the simplest media CDN setup with predictable delivery pricing.
providerRankings.launchUse: Use as alternate media CDN or future dedicated public audio delivery layer.
providerRankings.costPosture: Very cost-friendly for CDN delivery; monitor regional traffic.

providerRankings.name: AWS S3 + CloudFront
strengths: Industry-standard object storage and CDN stack.
Excellent durability, permissions, logging, lifecycle rules, and automation options.
Strong for companies already living inside AWS.
risks: Pricing has more moving parts: storage, requests, transfer, CloudFront delivery, logs, and optional features.
More configuration complexity than RKS3 needs at the current stage.
Billing mistakes can happen if caching and transfer rules are not controlled.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Powerful, but probably heavier than needed for the first RKS3 full-catalog audio deployment.
providerRankings.launchUse: Keep as a later enterprise path if RKS3 needs AWS-level controls or archival automation.
providerRankings.costPosture: Scalable but more complex; requires billing guardrails.

providerRankings.name: Supabase Storage
providerRankings.recommendedRole: Good if Supabase becomes the app backend
strengths: Storage buckets integrate with Supabase app architecture.
Fine-grained access controls fit membership features.
CDN caching is built into Supabase Storage delivery.
risks: Can become less ideal if RKS3's main need is pure high-bandwidth audio delivery.
Storage and egress limits should be watched closely.
May not be the cleanest primary home for 483+ HDWAV audio masters.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Use if Supabase becomes the RKS3 user/account/backend system. Not the first pick for primary HDWAV media CDN.
providerRankings.launchUse: Good for user assets, portal files, private member materials, or admin uploads.
providerRankings.costPosture: Good backend bundle; watch file storage and egress.

providerRankings.name: Vercel Blob
strengths: Supports public and private access modes.
Simple developer experience for app-managed files.
risks: Not the strongest primary choice for a growing HDWAV music catalog.
Can tie media storage too closely to the app hosting layer.
Need to monitor usage limits and pricing carefully.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Useful for app-level uploads, but do not make it the main RKS3 HDWAV catalog storage unless the catalog stays small.
providerRankings.launchUse: Use for portal images, admin assets, temporary uploads, or small protected files.
providerRankings.costPosture: Convenient but not the best long-term audio-catalog posture.

providerRankings.name: Git / Vercel public folder
strengths: Works for the current protected 30-record sample.
risks: Large audio should not be committed to Git.
Repository bloat breaks professional deployment hygiene.
Not built for 483+ HDWAV records or future 1,100+ record growth.
providerRankings.rks3Decision: Keep only for the active local 30-record sample during development. Do not use for full catalog deployment.
providerRankings.costPosture: Bad scale posture even if it appears free.

implementationPhases.title: Keep live portal protected
implementationPhases.action: Do not replace local sample audio yet. Keep the active 30-record portal stable.

implementationPhases.title: Choose provider
implementationPhases.action: Approve Cloudflare R2 as primary or Bunny as backup before uploading HDWAV audio.

implementationPhases.title: Create bucket/storage zone
implementationPhases.action: Create one storage container for public audio and reserve separate containers for private/member assets later.

implementationPhases.title: Design canonical media path
implementationPhases.action: Use stable URLs such as /audio/rks3/full/{category}/{slug}.wav through a custom media domain.

implementationPhases.title: Upload small pilot
implementationPhases.action: Upload 5 to 10 HDWAV files only, test playback, cache headers, browser loading, and mobile playback.

implementationPhases.title: Update metadata path strategy
implementationPhases.action: Generate external audioSrc values without changing source file names.

implementationPhases.title: Scale only after review
implementationPhases.action: Promote full catalog only after weak titles, duplicates, visibility, and storage policy are approved.
